title: SOC 2 common criteria, availability and confidentiality to Grundschutz++
description: The 33 common criteria (CC1.1 to CC9.2) of the AICPA Trust Services Criteria 2017 with the revised points of focus of 2022, the part every SOC 2 report covers, and the two categories most reports add: availability (A1.1 to A1.3) and confidentiality (C1.1, C1.2). Processing integrity and privacy (PI1, P1 to P8) are in the catalog but not mapped yet. Each criterion names the ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A controls it corresponds to; the Grundschutz++ targets of those controls come from the BSI's own mapping. Direct targets cover what Annex A lacks, notably governance and risk assessment (ISMS clauses 4 to 10). The step from each criterion to ISO and the direct targets are a draft written with AI assistance and not yet reviewed by a person; the AICPA's own mapping to ISO 27001 (2018) is for members only, predates ISO 27001:2022 and was not used. The criteria are the AICPA's: only their IDs are used here, every remark is our own wording.

source.title: AICPA Trust Services Criteria 2017 (revised points of focus 2022): common criteria, availability, confidentiality

maps.remarks: Tone at the top: a code of conduct, its acceptance in the terms of employment, and consequences for breaching it.

Oversight of internal control by a governing body independent of management. Annex A has the independent review; the governing body's approval and the report to it are ISMS clauses 5 and 9.3, direct targets.
Structures, reporting lines, authority and responsibility, set by management under the board's oversight.
Attracting, developing and keeping competent people: screening, terms, awareness and training.
Holding people accountable for their internal-control responsibilities.
Relevant, quality information to support internal control. Annex A has documented operating procedures; controlled documented information is ISMS clause 7.5.
Communicating objectives and responsibilities for internal control inside the organisation.
Communicating with external parties about matters that affect internal control.
Objectives specified clearly enough to identify and assess the risks to them. ISMS clauses 4.3 and 6.2, not Annex A.
Identifying and analysing risks to the objectives across the organisation. Risk assessment is ISMS clause 6.1; Annex A adds threat intelligence.
Considering the potential for fraud. Annex A has segregation of duties; insiders are a direct target.
Identifying and assessing changes, inside and outside, that could affect internal control. The context is ISMS clause 4.
Ongoing and separate evaluations of whether the controls are present and work. Annex A has the reviews; the audit programme is ISMS clause 9.2.
Evaluating deficiencies and reporting them in time to those who can correct them. ISMS clauses 9.3 and 10.
Choosing and developing control activities that bring risks down to an acceptable level: risk treatment, ISMS clause 6.1.3.
General control activities over technology: access, configuration, development and change.
Control activities put in place through policies and procedures.
Logical access security over protected information assets: inventory, access control, privileged rights, authentication and encryption.
Registering, authorising and deregistering users before credentials are issued.
Granting, changing and removing access by role, least privilege and segregation of duties.
Restricting physical access to facilities and protected assets.
Discontinuing protection only when assets are disposed of and data can no longer be recovered.
Protecting against threats from outside the system boundary: network controls and authentication of outside access.
Restricting and protecting information in transmission, movement and removal.
Preventing or detecting unauthorised and malicious software.
Detecting configuration changes that introduce vulnerabilities, and new vulnerabilities.
Monitoring components for anomalies that indicate malicious acts, disasters or errors.
Evaluating security events to decide whether they are incidents.
Responding to identified incidents: containment, remediation and communication.
Recovering from identified incidents.
Authorising, designing, developing, testing, approving and implementing changes.
Identifying and developing risk-mitigation activities for business disruption.
Assessing and managing risks from vendors and business partners.
Keeping capacity in line with demand, so that the availability commitments can be met.
Environmental protections, software, data backup and recovery infrastructure to meet the availability commitments.
Testing the recovery plan procedures that support system recovery. Annex A has ICT readiness for continuity; the tests themselves are direct targets.
Identifying confidential information and keeping it protected for as long as it is confidential.
Disposing of confidential information when it is no longer needed. Annex A has deletion and disposal; retention periods are a direct target.
